message:
## Vulnerability Digest

No new, credible vulnerabilities were found in the last 24 hours that could be matched to the normalized DLL/component inventory.

**Scope:** `DLL_software_component.txt` only. Duplicate package names, NuGet labels, capitalization variants, and product-family aliases were normalized within that file. `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` were not read or combined.

**Scan window:** 2026-10-14 07:40 UTC through 2026-10-15 07:40 UTC (2026-10-14 13:10 IST through 2026-10-15 13:10 IST).

### Findings

No relevant findings survived the freshness, product-match, and source-credibility checks.

The two newly published NuGet advisories visible for October 14 affected `Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers` (CVE-2026-72923) and `Metalama.Framework` (CVE-2026-62847), neither of which is in this DLL inventory. Microsoft advisories affecting nearby .NET product families, including `System.Security.Cryptography.Xml`, were published October 13 and therefore fell outside this run's 24-hour window. [GitHub Advisory Database - NuGet](https://github.com/advisories?query=ecosystem%3Anuget+sort%3Apublished-desc)

### MongoDB ecosystem verification

A separate sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, official drivers and connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, vendor advisories, CVE/NVD results, GitHub Security Advisories, and CISA sources. No credible MongoDB-related vulnerability was newly reported inside this run's window. MongoDB's latest vendor-listed security advisories surfaced during the sweep were dated October 13, before the cutoff. [MongoDB Alerts](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts), [MongoDB GitHub security advisories](https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/security/advisories)

### Review priority

No immediate vulnerability review is indicated from new disclosures in this scan window. Continue normal monitoring; older known vulnerabilities and unsupported component versions were outside this freshness-only digest.
